# Pilot Detection Checklist

Status: Validated
Specification Version: v2
Frozen: true
Type: General
Current Pass: 2

## Commandment Scores

| Pass | Commandment | State | Score | Why | Why not 100% | Escalated | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scope | Stable | 85% | D1 fixes scope to manual-only pilot; owner explicitly declined automation. | Pilot boundary (when it ends / converts) not yet defined. | No | — |
| 1 | Stakeholders | Stable | 90% | Owner is sole named stakeholder; reporting team already runs the Friday review this reuses. | No secondary stakeholder (e.g. whoever consumes missed-alert findings) confirmed. | No | — |
| 1 | Constraints | Stable | 90% | Owner accepted 7-day detection delay and no-automation constraint as explicit tradeoffs (D1). | Delay upper bound accepted but not tied to a hard SLA elsewhere in the org. | No | — |
| 1 | Harmony | Stable | 80% | Initial pass; no conflicting sections yet since spec was mostly open. | Full requirements/validation layers not yet populated at time of this row. | No | — |
| 2 | Success | Stable | 95% | User explicitly defined "done" as: four items present + no automation introduced. | Success criteria are checklist-content-only; doesn't verify the Friday review is actually executed. | No | — |
| 2 | Verification | Stable | 90% | Two-Friday missed-alert inspection, owned by the user, serves as the in-progress signal. | Cadence is fixed at two weeks; no faster signal exists by design (accepted under D1). | No | — |
| 2 | Constraints | Stable | 95% | User restated D1 tradeoff unchanged: manual-only, 7-day delay accepted, no automation. | None material — restatement matches prior acceptance exactly. | No | — |
| 2 | Harmony | Stable | 90% | All sections now consistent: requirements, constraints, success, and validation all reference the same four elements (Friday review, 7-day delay, ownership, two-Friday check) with no contradiction. | Long-term evolution beyond the pilot (e.g. what happens after two Fridays if delay causes a miss) is intentionally out of scope, not resolved. | No | — |

## Problem Statement

Produce a checklist artifact documenting the reporting team's manual detection pilot: a Friday-cadence manual review process, with an explicitly accepted detection delay, named ownership, and a scheduled follow-up inspection. No systems or automation are to be introduced — this is a documentation deliverable only, formalizing an already-approved manual approach (D1).

## Requirements

### R1
The checklist must list the Friday manual review as the detection mechanism.

### R2
The checklist must state the accepted maximum detection delay of seven days.

### R3
The checklist must name the owner (the requesting user) as responsible for the review process.

### R4
The checklist must specify a follow-up inspection of missed alerts to occur after two Fridays have elapsed.

## Constraints

### C1
No automation may be introduced as part of this deliverable or its execution — decision D1, explicitly declined by the owner for this pilot.

### C2
The checklist is the only deliverable; no supporting systems, scripts, or tooling changes are in scope.

## Success Criteria

### S1
All four items (R1–R4) are present and explicitly stated in the checklist document.

### S2
No automation artifact (script, scheduled job, alerting rule, etc.) is introduced as part of delivering the checklist.

## Validation Contract

### Acceptance Tests
- Checklist document contains an explicit line/section for the Friday review (R1).
- Checklist document states the seven-day accepted detection delay (R2).
- Checklist document names the owner as responsible (R3).
- Checklist document specifies the two-Friday missed-alert inspection (R4).
- Repository/workspace diff introduces no automation code, config, or scheduled task (C1, S2).

### Regression Checks
- Re-inspect the checklist after any future edit to confirm none of R1–R4 were silently dropped.
- Confirm no automation was introduced incidentally by any downstream tooling change (e.g. accidental script generation).

### Failure Signals
- Checklist missing any of the four required items.
- Presence of any automation artifact (script, cron job, alert rule) tied to this pilot.

### Verification Methods
- Manual read-through of the checklist against R1–R4 (owner or reviewer).
- Diff review confirming no automation-related files were added.

### Feedback Loop Design
- **In-progress signal**: the owner's own two-Friday missed-alert inspection (R4) serves as the mid-flight signal that the manual process is or isn't catching what it should.
- **Cost/cadence**: biweekly (every two Fridays), borne entirely as the owner's manual review time — no tooling cost, consistent with the no-automation constraint.
- **Fallback**: if the two-Friday inspection surfaces missed alerts attributable to the 7-day delay, the owner escalates to reconsidering automation for the pilot (this reconsideration is out of scope for this checklist itself, but the fallback path is explicitly named here).

### Known Blind Spots
- The checklist validates its own content correctness (R1–R4 present) but does not itself verify that the Friday review is actually being performed each week — that's an execution-time concern, not a spec-time one.
- No mechanism defined for what happens if the owner is unavailable on a given Friday; explicitly out of scope for this pilot per D1.

## Inputs
- Existing manual Friday review process (already running, unchanged).
- Owner's explicit tradeoff decision (D1): accept 7-day delay, decline automation, self-assign review after two Fridays.

## Outputs
- A single checklist document listing R1–R4.

## Out of Scope
- Any automation, tooling, or systems change.
- Redefining or improving the Friday review process itself.
- SLA negotiation beyond the 7-day delay already accepted.

## Authority Boundaries

### Executor May Decide
- Formatting/structure of the checklist document (e.g. markdown list vs. table), as long as R1–R4 are all present.

### Executor Must Escalate
- Any temptation to add automation, tooling, or systems changes — must go back to the owner, since D1 explicitly declined this.

### Executor Must Not Change
- The four required checklist items (R1–R4) or the underlying tradeoff (7-day delay, manual-only, owner assignment, two-Friday cadence) without a new owner decision superseding D1.

## Current Interpretation

The task is to produce a checklist document — not a system, script, or process change — that faithfully records an already-approved manual detection pilot: Friday review as the mechanism, seven days as the accepted detection delay, the requesting user as owner, and a two-Friday-later inspection of missed alerts as the feedback mechanism. Success is purely about the checklist's content completeness and the absence of any automation artifact.

## Misclassification Risks

### Potential False Positives
- A checklist that lists all four items in vague or non-actionable language (e.g. "review happens sometime") could pass a surface-level check while failing to actually convey the operational commitments.

### Potential False Negatives
- Missing acceptance test coverage for wording precision could let a technically-complete-but-vague checklist ship undetected.

## Ambiguities

### Blocking
_None — all four required items and constraints have been explicitly confirmed by the user._

### Non-Blocking
- Long-term pilot boundary (when/if this converts to automation) is undefined but intentionally deferred.

### Intentional
- No SLA beyond 7-day delay is defined — accepted tradeoff under D1.
- No automation fallback is designed in detail beyond naming it as an escalation path.

## Risks
- Detection delay of up to 7 days could allow issues to persist longer than automated detection would; explicitly accepted by the owner as a pilot tradeoff.
- Owner unavailability on a given Friday is not addressed and could silently extend the delay further.

## Stakeholders
- Owner (requesting user): responsible for the Friday review and the two-Friday missed-alert inspection.
- Reporting team: executes the existing manual Friday review that this checklist formalizes.
</spec>
